findings.claim: {"class":"CRASH_UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION","secondary":["PERFORMANCE_DEGRADATION"],"description":"Reporter (issue #2474, 'Charset sniffing can fail if advisory available() throws on JDK 8 HttpURLConnection'), in their own words: 'There's an issue in the charset sniffing path where jsoup could abort parsing if an advisory available() call throws an IOException. On the legacy JDK 8 HttpURLConnection, available() can throw IOException: Stream closed after the peer has closed the socket. In this path, jsoup was only using available() as a hint to speed optimize charset detection, so that exception was too strong a signal... I found this while chasing a flaky ConnectTest.maxBodySize failure on JDK 8 Ubuntu CI. The stack ended up in charset sniffing, and the exception was coming from InputStream.available(), not from an actual body read.' No verbatim stack-trace text was quoted in the issue body (commentCount: 0, no discussion thread). Diff-confirmed at both touched files: SimpleBufferedInput.fill() previously called `if (in.available() < 1) break;` unguarded inside its opportunistic-refill loop; the fix wraps it in try/catch(IOException), breaking (and keeping already-buffered bytes) instead of letting the IOException propagate. SimpleStreamReader.read(char[],int,int) previously called `!(in.available() > 0)` unguarded inline in its decode-underflow branch; the fix extracts this into a new private hasAvailableBytes() that catches IOException and returns false. Both call sites are in the charset-sniffing / stream-decoding path that DataUtil uses on parse, matching the reporter's description.","entryPoint":{"fqcn":"org.jsoup.internal.SimpleStreamReader","name":"read","descriptor":"([CII)I","sourceFile":"src/main/java/org/jsoup/internal/SimpleStreamReader.java"},"confidence":0.75,"verbatimStackTracePresent":false,"gaps":[{"reason":"NoSymptom","detail":"Issue text narrates the failure ('stack ended up in charset sniffing') but does not quote a verbatim stack trace or exception message text, so the exact throw site (SimpleBufferedInput.fill vs SimpleStreamReader.read) cannot be distinguished from the report alone -- only from the diff."}]}

findings.claim: {"class":"CRASH_UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION","secondary":["RESOURCE_LEAK"],"description":"Commit message: 'Apply the default 512 max stack depth to the XML parser (#2570)'. No linked issue and no separate reporter narrative -- forge_issue(2570) resolves to the PR itself with an empty body. Diff-confirmed: at the parent commit, XmlTreeBuilder overrode `int defaultMaxDepth()` to return `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, i.e. effectively unbounded recursion/stack growth for deeply nested XML input, unlike the HTML tree builder which uses TreeBuilder's bounded default. The fix commit removes this override entirely, so XmlTreeBuilder now inherits the same default max-depth guard (checked via the existing enforceStackDepthLimit() call inside insertElementFor) that the HTML parser already had. This is a crash-prevention fix: without it, sufficiently deeply nested XML (e.g. many thousands of nested elements) could exhaust the JVM call stack (StackOverflowError) during recursive tree-building or serialization, since nothing capped how deep the open-element stack could grow.","entryPoint":{"fqcn":"org.jsoup.parser.XmlTreeBuilder","name":"insertElementFor","descriptor":"(Lorg/jsoup/parser/Token$StartTag;)V","sourceFile":"src/main/java/org/jsoup/parser/XmlTreeBuilder.java"},"confidence":0.5,"verbatimStackTracePresent":false,"gaps":[{"reason":"NoLinkedIssue","detail":"PR #2570 has no distinct linked issue and an empty issue body; nothing beyond the commit/PR title describes an observed failure."},{"reason":"NoSymptom","detail":"No reporter ever demonstrated a StackOverflowError from deep XML nesting; the crash-prevention framing is inferred entirely from the removed Integer.MAX_VALUE override, not from an observed trace."}]}

findings.claim: {"class":"CRASH_UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION","description":"No PR, no linked issue, and no issueRefs at all on this commit -- history_commit_meta returns issueRefs: [] and forge_pr_for_commit returns Unknown(NotApplicable, 'no pull request associated'). Diff-confirmed: at the parent commit, Re2jRegex$Re2jMatcher#find() caught only `StackOverflowError` around the delegate re2j matcher's find() call, wrapping it into `ValidationException(PatternComplexityError)`; an OutOfMemoryError from the same complex-pattern-matching call would propagate uncaught instead of being normalized. findings.claim: {"class":"INCORRECT_OUTPUT","secondary":["API_CONTRACT_VIOLATION"],"description":"PR #2581 / commit message: 'Template end-tag and EOF processing now distinguish input created elements from the synthetic fragment context. This preserves the initial template insertion mode while allowing nested templates to close normally.' forge_issue(2581) resolves to the PR itself (labels: bug, fixed) with the same text and no separate reporter narrative or stack trace. Diff-confirmed at two sites in HtmlTreeBuilderState.java: (1) the InHead state's EndTag=\"template\" handler changed its stack-presence guard from `tb.onStack(name)` to `tb.onStackAboveContext(name)`; (2) the InTemplate state's EOF handler changed its guard from `tb.onStack(\"template\")` to `tb.onStackAboveContext(\"template\")` before popping/closing the template stack and resetting the insertion mode. onStack(name) matches any element with that name anywhere on the open-elements stack, including the synthetic context element used to seed a fragment parse (e.g. parseFragment with a <template> context element); onStackAboveContext excludes that synthetic context element. Before the fix, a fragment parse seeded with a template context could have its own synthetic context element mistaken for a real open <template>, causing the InHead end-tag handler to spuriously treat a top-level </template> as valid-and-poppable (or the reverse: tb.error(this) fired) and the InTemplate EOF handler to incorrectly believe there was still an input-created template to close, altering the resulting parse tree / insertion-mode state versus a correct parse. {"class":"INCORRECT_OUTPUT","description":"Reporter (issue #2503, filed by maintainer jhy) states: 'RCDATA elements like and <textarea> should match their end tags case-insensitively. A direct mixed-case closer works as expected: <title>Foo closes the title. But when tag-shaped text appears before the closer, jsoup can miss the mixed-case end tag and leave RCDATA early. For example, <p>Foo creates a real body p element instead of keeping

Foo as title text. Similarly, creates an img element.' Root cause per the report: 'This was a premature optimization: the implementation only looked for consistent-case matches.' i.e. parsing certain RCDATA content (title/textarea) with a mixed-case end tag preceded by tag-shaped text produces a wrong DOM tree (markup promoted out of what should remain literal RCDATA text), rather than an exception.","entryPoint":{"fqcn":"org.jsoup.Jsoup","name":"parse","descriptor":"(Ljava/lang/String;Ljava/lang/String;)Lorg/jsoup/nodes/Document;"},"confidence":0.55,"gaps":[{"reason":"NoDebugInfo","detail":"No stack trace or exception; symptom is a structural/output mismatch described in prose with example HTML snippets, not runnable reporter code, so the exact public entry call was not literally quoted by the reporter — Jsoup.parse(String,String) is inferred as the general HTML-parsing entry point that would exercise the described RCDATA tokenization path (whose implementation lives in CharacterReader.java, the file the fix touched). Issue has 0 comments, no further corroboration available."}]}

findings.subject: b035b623d3d1d0c50d84056d2946ba1a90f7f665
findings.claim: {"class":"API_CONTRACT_VIOLATION","secondary":["SECURITY_EXPOSURE"],"description":"StringUtil.resolve(URL,String) / resolve(String,String) would happily produce and return an absolute http(s):// URL string even when the resolved result had no host, contrary to RFC 9110's authority requirement for the http(s) schemes. Downstream, Safelist's protocol validation used this string form, so a malformed hostless http(s) value could be treated as satisfying an allowed http/https protocol and revived during Cleaner sanitization instead of being rejected. The fix commit message ('Make hostless HTTP(S) URLs fail resolution and cleaning') and PR body state: 'HTTP and HTTPS resolution now rejects results without a host in accordance with RFC 9110. The Safelist fallback preserves custom URI schemes without reviving malformed HTTP(S) values.' Diff-confirmed: the fix commit's StringUtil.java adds a private validateHttpUrl(URL) that throws MalformedURLException when isHttpScheme(protocol) && host.isEmpty(), called from both resolve(URL,String) and (transitively) resolve(String,String); resolve(String,String)'s catch-block fallback for a MalformedURLException now falls through to the validUriScheme/hasHttpScheme check that specifically excludes http(s) values from being revived as raw strings. There is no distinct bug-report issue -- PR #2579 is self-authored by the maintainer with no separate issue thread, and its 'issue' record is simply the PR itself (state MERGED, same text as the commit message), so this is a proactive spec-compliance fix rather than a triaged user report.","entryPoint":{"fqcn":"org.jsoup.internal.StringUtil","name":"resolve","descriptor":"(Ljava/lang/String;Ljava/lang/String;)Ljava/lang/String;","sourceFile":"src/main/java/org/jsoup/internal/StringUtil.java"},"confidence":0.55,"verbatimStackTracePresent":false,"gaps":[{"reason":"NoLinkedIssue","detail":"PR #2579 has no distinct linked issue; forge_pr_for_commit returned linkedIssues: [] and forge_issue(2579) resolves to the PR itself, not a separate bug report."},{"reason":"NoSymptom","detail":"No reporter-observed manifestation (e.g. a specific malformed URL or downstream failure) is on record; symptom is reconstructed purely from the diff and RFC-9110 framing in the commit/PR text."}]}
